body.statement:
For every regular coherent foldwise fit, let \(\widehat M_A\) and \(\widehat M_Z\) denote the raw measurement fits and let \(\bar M_A\) and \(\bar M_Z\) denote their threshold-and-renormalize cleanings.  Every fitted bridge and every fitted object \(\widehat B,\widehat d,\widehat D,\widehat R,\widehat N,\widehat h,\widehat G,\widehat b_{(\cdot)},\widehat Q\) is formed from \((\bar M_A,\bar M_Z)\), and \(\widehat m_j(x)=\int_{\mathcal Y}y\widehat f_j(y\mid x)d\nu(y)\).  With \(r_A^c=r_A+\tau_{S,n}\) and \(r_Z^c=r_Z+\tau_{S,n}\),
\[
 \{E_P\|\widehat N-N_B\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\}^{1/2}
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_D+r_B),
\]
\(r_R+r_N+r_h+r_G+r_b=O_P(R_\Sigma)\), and
\[
 \|\widehat Q\widehat U-QU\|_{L^2(P)}
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma.
\]
The full estimated efficient score \(\widehat U-\widehat Q\widehat U\) has the same linear \(L^2(P)\) stability bound relative to \(U-QU\).  In particular, the bridge perturbations use
\[
 \bar M_A^{-1}M_A-I_K=\bar M_A^{-1}(M_A-\bar M_A),
 \qquad
 \bar M_Z^{-1}M_Z-I_K=\bar M_Z^{-1}(M_Z-\bar M_Z),
\]
so the raw essential-supremum errors \(r_{A,\infty}\) and \(r_{Z,\infty}\) are screening quantities only, while \(r_B,\ldots,r_b\) are errors of the cleaned-law plug-ins.
body.justification: The revised stability proof uses barred measurement inverses and propagates only cleaned-law errors through the posterior and Gram maps.
body.gap: Existing bridge papers do not analyze perturbation of this support-cleaned nested projector.
body.consumer: It turns a coherent cleaned factor fit into stable efficient scores and covariance estimates.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(\|V\|_2=\{E_P\|V\|^2\}^{1/2}\), with the Euclidean, Frobenius, or operator norm according to the type of \(V\).  Constants below depend only on the quantities allowed in \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}\).  By the support-cleaning lemma,
\[
 \|\bar M_A-M_A\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A^c,
 \qquad
 \|\bar M_Z-M_Z\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_Z^c.                 \tag{41}
\]
These bounds hold whether or not the screening event occurs; that event is needed for exact recovery of zeros, not for stability.

Put
\[
 H=B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B,
 \qquad
 \widehat H=\widehat B^{\mathsf T}\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B,
 \qquad
 \widehat B=\bar M_A\odot\bar M_Z.                              \tag{42}
\]
Observed-cell positivity gives \(\|D^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\varepsilon^{-1}\), and the computable fitted half-margin gives \(\|\widehat D^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq2\varepsilon^{-1}\).  For \(v\in\mathbb R^K\), matricization and the Khatri--Rao definition yield
\[
 \operatorname{mat}(Bv)=M_A\operatorname{diag}(v)M_Z^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{mat}(\widehat Bv)=\bar M_A\operatorname{diag}(v)\bar M_Z^{\mathsf T}. \tag{43}
\]
The true singular-value margins and the fitted half-margins therefore imply
\[
 \|Bv\|_2\geq\varepsilon^2\|v\|_2,
 \qquad
 \|\widehat Bv\|_2\geq\frac{\varepsilon^2}{4}\|v\|_2.          \tag{44}
\]
Since the diagonal entries of \(D\) and \(\widehat D\) are probabilities and hence at most one,
\[
 v^{\mathsf T}Hv=\|D^{-1/2}Bv\|_2^2\geq\varepsilon^4\|v\|_2^2,
 \qquad
 v^{\mathsf T}\widehat Hv\geq\frac{\varepsilon^4}{16}\|v\|_2^2.
\]
Thus both matrices are invertible and
\[
 \|H^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\varepsilon^{-4},
 \qquad
 \|\widehat H^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq16\varepsilon^{-4}.      \tag{45}
\]

The exact identities
\[
 \widehat D^{-1}-D^{-1}=\widehat D^{-1}(D-\widehat D)D^{-1},
 \qquad
 \widehat H^{-1}-H^{-1}=\widehat H^{-1}(H-\widehat H)H^{-1}      \tag{46}
\]
and product telescoping in \(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B\) give
\[
 \|\widehat H-H\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}
 \bigl(\|\widehat B-B\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\|\widehat D-D\|_{\mathrm{op}}\bigr). \tag{47}
\]
Applying (46)--(47) to
\[
 N_B=I_{K^2}-D^{-1}BH^{-1}B^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \widehat N=I_{K^2}-\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B\widehat H^{-1}\widehat B^{\mathsf T}
\]
gives pointwise
\[
 \|\widehat N-N_B\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}
 \bigl(\|\widehat D-D\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\|\widehat B-B\|_{\mathrm{op}}\bigr). \tag{48}
\]
Taking the declared conditional \(L^2(P)\) norm proves the first displayed assertion.

The cleaned inverse-feature bridges satisfy the exact identities
\[
 \bar M_A^{-1}M_A-I_K=\bar M_A^{-1}(M_A-\bar M_A),
 \qquad
 \bar M_Z^{-1}M_Z-I_K=\bar M_Z^{-1}(M_Z-\bar M_Z).               \tag{49}
\]
The fitted singular-value half-margins and (41) consequently bound the two conditional bridge-mean errors by \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A^c\) and \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_Z^c\).  The fitted outcome regression is not an independently chosen nuisance: bounded support and its definition from \(\widehat f\) give \(|\widehat m_j|\leq L\).  Product telescoping in the raw bridge formula, latent positivity, and the fitted propensity half-margin then give
\[
 \|\widehat U-U\|_2
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_m+r_\pi+r_A^c+r_Z^c)
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma.                                \tag{50}
\]

For the conditional Gram step, the established data-driven Gram-threshold lemma, applied with \(\tau_G=\varepsilon/2\), yields
\[
 \|\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}-G^+\|_{L^2(P_X;\mathrm{op})}
 \leq26\varepsilon^{-2}r_G,
 \qquad
 \|\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq2\varepsilon^{-1}.                                        \tag{51}
\]
Every map preceding this solve is evaluated at the cleaned product law.  Conditional expectation is an \(L^2\)-contraction, and the inverse identity (46), its measurement analogue (49), and finite product telescoping show successively that the errors of \(\widehat B,\widehat d,\widehat D,\widehat R,\widehat N,\widehat c,\widehat h,\widehat G\), and \(\widehat b_{(\cdot)}\) are precisely the cleaned-law coordinates \(r_B,r_d,r_D,r_R,r_N,r_h,r_G,r_b\).  All undifferenced factors are bounded by the true and fitted margins.  In particular,
\[
 r_R+r_N+r_h+r_G+r_b\leq R_\Sigma,                              \tag{52}
\]
which proves the asserted \(O_P(R_\Sigma)\) relation.  Notice that neither \(r_{A,\infty}\) nor \(r_{Z,\infty}\) appears in (50)--(52); those two errors enter only the screening ratio \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}\).

Let \(\widehat b_{\widehat U}\) be the right-hand side formed from the same cleaned fitted law and \(\widehat U\).  Adding and subtracting one factor at a time gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\widehat h^{\mathsf T}\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}\widehat b_{\widehat U}
   -h^{\mathsf T}G^+b_U\\
 &=(\widehat h-h)^{\mathsf T}\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}\widehat b_{\widehat U}
   +h^{\mathsf T}(\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}-G^+)\widehat b_{\widehat U}
   +h^{\mathsf T}G^+(\widehat b_{\widehat U}-b_U).
\end{aligned}                                                    \tag{53}
\]
Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz, (51), and the uniform margin bounds imply
\[
 \|\widehat h^{\mathsf T}\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}\widehat b_{\widehat U}
   -h^{\mathsf T}G^+b_U\|_2
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_h+r_G+r_b)
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma.                                \tag{54}
\]
Likewise, (48) and (50) imply
\[
 \|\widehat N\widehat U-N_BU\|_2
 \leq\|(\widehat N-N_B)\widehat U\|_2+\|N_B(\widehat U-U)\|_2
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma.                                \tag{55}
\]
Subtracting (54) from (55) according to the definitions of \(\widehat Q\) and \(Q\) proves
\[
 \|\widehat Q\widehat U-QU\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma. \tag{56}
\]
Finally,
\[
 (\widehat U-\widehat Q\widehat U)-(U-QU)
 =(\widehat U-U)-(\widehat Q\widehat U-QU),
\]
so (50), (56), and the triangle inequality prove the last assertion.
